big-statement.description: One sentence, huge and centered in the primary colour: the line the audience must remember ("You can revert the program."). Markup, not a layout: never write `layout: statement`.
big-statement.body: You can revert the program.

big-quote.description: A sourced quote, huge and centered. Only with verbatim words from a source you read this run. Markup, not a layout: never write `layout: quote`.
big-quote.body: "This was a catastrophic failure on my part… I destroyed months of work in seconds."

section-opener.description: Section opener with the line graphics: a question from the story spine, or an act title. Markup, not a layout: never write `layout: section`.
section-opener.body: Pulumi Neo in the terminal.

full-image.description: Full-bleed picture or GIF. This one pattern uses a layout (`layout: image`, in its frontmatter). The file goes under public/; use only images you may use.

quote-card.description: The incident: the source's words in a card, three facts beside it, a reveal line underneath.
quote-card.body:
# An AI said that. About a production database.
The agent's own words

"This was a catastrophic failure on my part… I destroyed months of work in seconds."

  • A founder testing "vibe coding" live, in public
  • Mid code freeze, told not to proceed without approval
  • It also said rollback was impossible. That wasn't true.
Psssst… it was Replit's own agent, July 2025

compare.description: Two cards side by side: before and after, then and now, a codebase against your cloud.
compare.body:
# What changes when the target is your cloud
A codebase
  • Review a diff
  • Revert with one command
  • Tests run on fakes
Your cloud
  • Review a preview against live state
  • Deletes are permanent
  • Tests run in real accounts

zones.description: Two zones joined by an arrow, with a callout underneath: where things run, what reaches what.

options.description: Three option cards with a visual track: modes, levels, tiers.

flow.description: Numbered steps joined by arrows, with a callout: a process or a lifecycle. Use it instead of a diagram.

chain.description: A request or identity chain, node to node, with a summary line.

terminal.description: A terminal window listing commands or flags; the ones the demo uses are highlighted.

stack.description: Pieces that stack into a whole (layers, add-ons), with a legend beside them.

boundaries.description: Rows of 'this is guarded by that', with icons and arrows.

demo-overview.description: What we are going to do: one card per demo step.

demo-step.description: A numbered demo step: the commands in big-code blocks, what to watch for as an icon list. Keep each fact's text inside its <span>: inline code outside it breaks the line apart.
demo-step.body:
# 1 · One secret, one kit, one shell
host
```bash sbx secret ls sbx rm -f neo-demo sbx run --name neo-demo --kit ./01-sandbox/region-kit \ ghcr.io/dirien/infrastructure-sandbox-kit:v0.10.0 ./02-app ```
sandbox shell
```bash pulumi whoami -v echo "$PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN" # proxy-managed ```
  • First run pulls the image
  • And asks to approve the binding
  • The kit's install step is a no-op
  • Then a shell opens in the VM

demo-checks.description: A numbered demo step with one command and a grid of numbered checks.

demo-outcome.description: A numbered demo step with the prompt, a flow of what happens, the code that matters and a callout.
